The Confederation of African Football has pledged to implement the Court of Arbitration for Sport’s ruling restoring Senegal as champions of the 2025 Africa Cup of Nations. CAF, in a statement published on its website on Tuesday, said it respected the verdict, which overturned its Appeals Board’s decision to strip Senegal of the continental title and award it to Morocco. It said the CAS panel had set aside the decision of CAF’s Appeals Board, which stripped Senegal of the title and awarded Morocco a 3-0 victory, while upholding the earlier decision of the CAF Disciplinary Board. “The CAS Panel ruled as follows: The Decision of the CAF Appeal Board of 17 March 2026 is set aside. “The Decision of the CAF Disciplinary Board of 11 February 2026 is confirmed. “Senegal has therefore been declared by CAS as the Winner of the TotalEnergies CAF Africa Cup of Nations Morocco 2025,” the statement read. The dispute stemmed from the controversial final played on January 18 at the Prince Moulay Abdellah Stadium in Rabat, where Senegal initially defeated hosts Morocco 1-0 after extra time to win their second continental title. The match descended into controversy in stoppage time after the referee awarded Morocco a penalty following a VAR review, shortly after Senegal had a goal disallowed. Angered by the decision, Senegal coach Pape Thiaw instructed his players to leave the pitch in protest. They returned after about 14 minutes, allowing the match to continue. AFCON: Morocco rejects verdict, alleges Senegal FA chief phoned CAS arbitrator CAS restores Senegal as 2025 AFCON champions AFCON dispute: Morocco accuses Senegal FA chief of contacting CAS arbitrator Morocco’s Brahim Diaz subsequently missed the penalty, while Pape Gueye scored the decisive goal in extra time to secure Senegal’s victory. Morocco later lodged a complaint with CAF, arguing that Senegal’s withdrawal had disrupted the normal course of the match. CAF’s Disciplinary Board initially allowed the result to stand while imposing sanctions on both teams over incidents during the final. However, its Appeals Board overturned that decision on March 17 and awarded Morocco the title. Senegal rejected the decision and appealed to CAS on March 25, seeking to have the original result restored. In its ruling on Tuesday, CAS held that the AFCON regulations invoked by CAF were not applicable to the circumstances of the match because the referee had allowed play to resume after Senegal’s players returned to the pitch. “AFCON Regulations are intended solely to determine the outcome of a match when a team’s conduct leads the referee to call off the game permanently. They are therefore not applicable in this case,” the panel ruled, according to a statement shared by Sky Sports reporter Rob Harris. The Royal Moroccan Football Federation has, however, rejected the CAS verdict and vowed to pursue further legal action. In a statement published on its X handle on Tuesday, the Moroccan federation also renewed its allegation that Senegalese Football Federation President Abdoulaye Fall had contacted German arbitrator Ulrich Haas, one of the three members of the CAS panel, 48 hours before the ruling. The Senegalese federation had denied the allegation, with its Secretary-General, Sow, describing it as “an imaginary appeal” and saying Fall did not know the judges and was not present at the hearing. Morocco’s rejection of the ruling came after CAS restored Senegal’s original 1-0 victory, ending months of uncertainty over the winner of the 2025 continental tournament.
